comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh 1 November 2026: the current ME regulations portal links the same adopted BSc OER. Appendix3 still prints KT2755 at4.5EC and year2=61EC, hence60+61+60=181 againstArt7degree180. A current official alternative was found: MScTechnicalMedicine2026–2027 Appendix2 lists the samecodeKT2755 at3.5EC in its36.5EC bridging programme. That is contemporary contrary evidence, but it governs a separate bridging programme and does not state that it corrects the BSc allocation or specify shared-credit rules. The linked public study-guide target returns404. Historical2024chart/olderOER cannot establish current BSc credits. Preserve all27diagnostic components,firstyear60 andthirdyear60; do not infer a one-credit reduction. Formal Art12c confirmsplacement requiresKT1905/equivalent andvaccination,andKTOrequiresallfirstyearplus≥53secondyearEC. No complete external path or UCR academic disposition verified.

exception.reason: The current bachelor OER specifies a 180-EC degree but its printed requirements total 181 EC. It assigns 4.5 EC to KT2755, while the current master bridging regulation lists that same code at 3.5 EC. No applicable correction or authoritative bachelor credit-sharing resolution has been established. The first year’s 60 EC is verified; complete reconstruction and UCR assessment remain incomplete. This is not an academic no-match.

audience.programmeDescription: Clinical Technology combines medicine and engineering to study the human body, disease and medical technology. The joint programme includes integrated medical and technical subjects, clinical and communication skills, design work, a healthcare placement and a research or design capstone.
